title: Structured batch proxy for OTLP HTTP -> Tempo with atomic ack semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a lightweight HTTP proxy that accepts OTLP/HTTP span batches from SDKs and downstream services and forwards them to Tempo with structured batching and atomic acknowledgment semantics. The proxy must: 1) accept OTLP/HTTP JSON and protobuf envelopes and normalize to internal canonical batch format, 2) persist batches to a local write-ahead buffer (durable filesystem queue) to survive short node restarts, 3) forward batches to Tempo using existing /api/traces endpoint with configurable max batch size and concurrency, 4) expose an ACK to the upstream only after the batch is durably accepted by either Tempo or the durable queue (atomic ack), 5) surface per-tenant backpressure metrics (queue_depth, inflight_batches, dropped_batches) and a health endpoint for graceful shedding, 6) degrade gracefully to a lightweight sampling-only mode under sustained overload, and 7) include compatibility transforms for Jaeger/Zipkin envelope fields (trace_id padding, span.tags mapping). Deliverables: design doc, unit+integration tests with Tempo mock, load benchmark results, Grafana dashboards for the new metrics, migration plan for customers switching from direct OTLP ingestion to the proxy.
comments: 2026-02-25 Aisha Patel: Ticket created after customer incidents where upstream SDKs saw 5xx spikes during Tempo maintenance. Goal is to provide atomic ack behavior so SDKs don't drop events on transient backend blips.

2026-02-27 Design review: Diego, Lila (SRE), and Marco (Runtime) walked the design. Agreed on WAL file-per-batch approach to keep ordering simple and reduce GC pressure. Action: Diego to prototype queue format and expose queue_depth metric.

2026-03-02 Diego Navarro: Prototype done (branch: eng/otlp-atomic-acks). WAL implementation uses segmented files with CRC checks and a small index shard for quick recovery. Benchmarked local fs persist at ~12k batches/s on i3.large using synthetic payloads.

2026-03-04 Lila Singh (SRE): Concern about file descriptor usage for many small batches; recommended limiting open segments to N and using mmap on Linux for reads. Also suggested soft limit alerts for queue_depth and a circuit-breaker to trigger sampling-only mode.

2026-03-06 Diego Navarro: Addressed fd usage by adding segment cache LRU and a configurable open_files cap. Added sampling-only fallback and prometheus metrics: proxy_queue_depth, proxy_inflight_batches, proxy_ack_latency_seconds_bucket, proxy_dropped_batches_total.

2026-03-08 QA: Integration tests added with a Tempo mock that simulates 500ms-3s tail latency and intermittent 503s. Verified that ACK is delayed until batch is persisted; upstream clients see stable 202/200 responses even when Tempo is flaky.

2026-03-10 PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-proxy/pull/412 (prototype -> staging). Includes unit tests, integration harness, and initial Grafana dashboard JSON. Requesting runtime review from Marco and SRE sign-off from Lila.

2026-03-11 Marco Alvarez (Runtime): Noted kernel-level optimizations for network send path could further reduce ack latency; suggested capping max_concurrency to avoid head-of-line blocking. Also requested an opt-in config for tenants that need strict ordering vs higher throughput.

2026-03-12 Diego Navarro: Merged changes on branch, running canary in eu-west-1 ingress for low-traffic tenants. Monitoring dashboard (grafana link below) created and alerting rules added for queue_depth>1000 for 5m and ack_latency P95 > 2s.

Next steps: finish documentation, run 72h canary with failure injection, and add migration playbook for customers. Post-merge action: add e2e smoke to platform CI that exercises the durable queue recovery path.
